Rashi on Gittin 62a:10:1.hebrew: בכלים של עמי הארץ - שאין מקבלין טומאה, הראויים להשתמש בהן חבר:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:10:1.english: In vessels of amei ha'aretz - that do not contract ritual impurity, [and are thus] fit for a chaver to use:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:11:2.hebrew: ואין כופלין - דהא דנותנים שלום לעובד כוכבים מפני דרכי שלום הוא דשרי, ומשום דרכי שלום בחדא זימנא סגי:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:11:2.english: And one may not double [the greeting] - for [the fact] that we extend shalom [a greeting] to an idolater is [only] permitted because of the ways of peace, and because of the ways of peace, one time suffices:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:11:3.hebrew: למימרא להו אחזוקו - כשאומרין לעושי מלאכה העוברים עליהם, "תחזקנה ידיכם":
Rashi on Gittin 62a:11:3.english: To say to them, "Be strong" - When passersby say to those doing work, "May your hands be strengthened":

Rashi on Gittin 62a:11:4.hebrew: אשרתא - אף הוא לשון חיזוק, כמו "אישרנוהי" (כתובות דף כא.):
Rashi on Gittin 62a:11:4.english: Asharta [well done] - This too is an expression of strengthening [and encouragement], like [the expression] isharnuhi ["we have confirmed/validated it"] (Ketubot 21a):

Rashi on Gittin 62a:12:1.hebrew: שלמא למר - ולא היה מתכוין לברכו, אלא לבו היה לרבו:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:12:1.english: Peace to [my] master - And he did not intend to bless him, rather his heart [was directed] toward his [own] teacher:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:13:1.hebrew: השתא אחזוקי מחזקינן - ידיהם בדבורא, בדבר האסור לישראל, כגון עבודת שביעית:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:13:1.english: Now [that] we strengthen - their hands verbally, in a matter that is forbidden to a Jew, such as work of the Sabbatical year:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:13:2.english: We greet them - [on] all days of the year, is it necessary [to state that]?

Rashi on Gittin 62a:13:3.english: On their festival day - and we are not concerned lest he go and give thanks [to his idol]:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:13:4.hebrew: לא יכנס כו' - דכיון דאחשביה כולי האי, דלמא אזיל ומודי:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:13:4.english: He may not enter, etc. - For since he treated him as so important, perhaps he [the gentile] will go and give thanks [to his deity]:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:14:1.english: Bar oryan - A son of Torah:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:14:2.hebrew: פלגאה - חולק על החכמים, שהיה מצערו למר עוקבא שהיה אב בית דין, כדאמרי' בפרק קמא (לעיל גיטין דף ז.):
Rashi on Gittin 62a:14:2.english: An argumentative person - [One who] disputes with the Sages, for he used to distress Mar Ukva, who was the head of the court, as we say in the first chapter (above, Gittin 7a):

Rashi on Gittin 62a:1:1.english: She may give her - Apparently, the wife of an am ha'aretz is suspected of stealing from her husband's [food] and giving [it] to her friend:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:2:1.english: She rules - She issues a ruling of permissibility for herself:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:1.hebrew: העיד ר' יוסי כו' - ברייתא היא:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:1.english: Rabbi Yosei testified, etc. - It is a baraita:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:2.hebrew: אין עושין חלת עם הארץ בטהרה - עם הארץ שאמר לגבל חבר: "הפרש חלה מעיסתי ועשה אותה בטהרה", לא ישמע לו, שהרי כבר נטמאה כל העיסה ביד עם הארץ, והכהן יסמוך על הגבל שהוא חבר, ויהא סבור שהחלה טהורה:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:2.english: One may not prepare challah for an am ha'aretz in [a state of] ritual purity - [If] an am ha'aretz said to a kneader [who is] a chaver, "Separate challah from my dough and prepare it in [a state of] ritual purity," he should not listen to him, for the entire dough has already become ritually impure in the hand of the am ha'aretz, and the kohen will rely on the kneader, who is a chaver, and will think that the challah is ritually pure:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:3.english: But they may prepare - the beginning of the dough in [a state of] ritual purity:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:4.hebrew: בכפישא או באנחותא - כלים של בלאי חמתות, ואין רגילים ליתן בהם עיסה, וטומאה אין מקבלין:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:4.english: In a kefisha or in an anchuta - [These are] vessels made of worn-out leather skins, and people do not ordinarily place dough in them, and they do not contract ritual impurity:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:5.hebrew: ואינו חושש - הגבל, שמא יגע עם הארץ בחלה ויטמאנה, ולקמיה מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:3:5.english: And he is not concerned - [i.e.,] the kneader [is not concerned] lest the am ha'aretz touch the challah and render it ritually impure; and further on [the Gemara] explains the reason:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:4:1.hebrew: ואין עושין תרומת זיתיו בטהרה - לאחר שהפך זיתים לתתן לבית הבד, אין מפרישים בדדים חבירים תרומה מהן לעשותן בטהרה, לפי שכבר הוכשרו במעטן ונטמאו, והכהן סומך עליהם וסובר שהן טהורים:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:4:1.english: And they do not prepare the terumah of his olives in ritual purity - After [the am ha'aretz] has turned the olives to put them into the olive press, olive-pressers [who are] chaverim may not separate terumah from them to prepare them in ritual purity, because they have already been rendered susceptible [to impurity] in the olive-vat and have become ritually impure, and the kohen relies upon them and thinks that they are ritually pure:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:5:1.hebrew: וטעמא מאי - שרו רבנן לאקולי בתרומה כי האי קולא, דאיכא למיחש דלמא הדר נגע:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:5:1.english: And what is the reason - [that] the Rabbis permitted being lenient with terumah with such a leniency, where there is concern lest he touch [it] again:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:6:1.hebrew: דלא נפיש אגריה - ששכרו מועט, לפיכך הוא עני וצריך למזונות:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:6:1.english: That his payment is not great - [Meaning] that his wage is small; therefore he is poor and in need of sustenance:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:6:2.hebrew: דלא שכיח - להשתכר כי אם משנה לשנה, להכי צריך למזונות:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:6:2.english: [Because] it is not common - to earn a living except from year to year; therefore, he needs [assistance] for sustenance:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:7:1.english: Because we say - [This is said] to intimidate him:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:7:2.english: If you touch it - and render it [ritually] impure:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:7:3.english: It reverts to [the status of] tevel [untithed produce] - and he [the am ha'aretz] is not suspected of eating tevel, which is punishable by death:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:8:1.english: He intends to prepare [it] properly - for he came to him to prepare it [properly] for him:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:8:2.english: He does not care - [This is said] as a rhetorical question:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:9:2.hebrew: איכא היכרא - שהניחה בכלים שאין עשויין להניח בהן עיסה, ונזכר על שאיימנו עליו:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:9:2.english: There is a conspicuous marker - Because he placed it [the challah] in vessels that are not made for holding dough, and [the am ha'aretz] is reminded of what we warned him about:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:9:3.english: What conspicuous marker is there - [for him] so that he will remember [not to touch it]:

Rashi on Gittin 62a:9:4.hebrew: בכלי גללים - שאינן מקבלים טומאה, דאי נגע בכלי לא מקבל טומאה, ובעיסה גופה אית ליה היכרא משום הני כלים שאינו רגיל להשתמש בהן, ועם הארץ לא אחמור רבנן עליה כולי האי לשוייה כזב גמור לטמא במשא:
Rashi on Gittin 62a:9:4.english: In dung vessels - which do not contract ritual impurity: for if he [the am ha'aretz] touches the vessel, it does not contract impurity, and regarding the dough [i.e., the terumah] itself, he has a conspicuous marker because of these vessels, which he is not accustomed to using; and the Rabbis were not so stringent regarding an am ha'aretz as to treat him like a full zav to impart impurity through carrying:

Tosafot on Gittin 62a:11:1.hebrew: אין עודרין עם העכו"ם בשביעית - והא דקאמר בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כו.) גבי כהן וחורש: "יכול לומר לו אגיסטון אני בתוכה", לא כמו שפי' בקונטרס "שכיר לנכרי", דהא משמע הכא דאסור, ולא מסתבר לחלק בין חנם לבשכר. אלא מפר"ת: אגיסטון — בקרקע שמקבלים מן המלך לפרוע כך וכך תבואה בשנה, כדאמר התם לעיל מינה: רבי ינאי מכריז "פוקו וזרעו ארנונא בשביעית"; ושמא סכנת נפשות איכא אם לא יפרעו מס למלך, אי נמי קסבר יש קנין לנכרי בארץ להפקיע משביעית, אי נמי שביעית בזמן הזה דרבנן — אע"ג דמדרבנן אסור לנכרי אחר, גבי מלך התירו:
Tosafot on Gittin 62a:11:1.english: One may not hoe with a gentile during the Sabbatical [Year] - And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 26a), regarding a priest who is plowing, "He can say to him, 'I am an agiston [tenant farmer] on it'" — [this is] not as Rashi explained, "a hired laborer for a gentile," for here it implies that it is forbidden, and it is not reasonable to distinguish between [working] for free and for wages. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam explains: An agiston [works] on land that they lease from the king to pay such-and-such [an amount of] grain per year, as [the Gemara] says there, just above that: "Rabbi Yannai proclaimed: Go out and sow [for] the arnona [royal tax] in the Sabbatical [Year]." And perhaps there is a danger to life if they do not pay the tax to the king; alternatively, [the Gemara] holds that a gentile has [the power of] acquisition in the Land [of Israel] to exempt [it] from [the laws of] the Sabbatical [Year]; alternatively, the Sabbatical [Year] in the present time is [only] rabbinic — even though by rabbinic law it is forbidden for another gentile, regarding the king they permitted [it]:

Tosafot on Gittin 62a:11:2.hebrew: אשרתא - בירושלמי איכא למאן דאמר דהיינו "חרש בה טבאות ולבתר שמיטה נסיבא לה מינך", ולישראל אמרינן "יישר"; ואיכא למ"ד דלעכו"ם אמר "יישר", ולישראל "שלום עליכם". משמע דלכ"ע לעכו"ם אסור לומר "שלום עליך", ודלא כש"ס שלנו הכא, דלא אסרינן לעובד כוכבים אלא כפילת שלום. ונראה דלפי' הירושלמי, דמחזיקים ידי נכרים בשביעית ושואלים בשלומם חדא מילתא היא, שאומר לו "חרש בה טבאות":
Tosafot on Gittin 62a:11:2.english: Asharta [Well done] - In the Yerushalmi there is one who says that this means: "Plow it well, and after the Sabbatical year I will take it from you," and to a Jew we say "Yishar" [well done]; and there is one who says that to a gentile he says "Yishar," and to a Jew "Shalom aleikhem" [peace be upon you]. This implies that according to everyone, it is forbidden to say "Shalom alekha" [peace be upon you] to a gentile — unlike our Talmud here, where we only forbid doubling "Shalom" to an idolater. And it appears that according to the explanation of the Yerushalmi, [the Mishnah's statements] "we strengthen the hands of gentiles in the Sabbatical year" and "we inquire after their peace" are one and the same thing, namely that he says to him, "Plow it well":

Tosafot on Gittin 62a:12:1.hebrew: שלמא למר - פי' בקונטרס, ולא היה מתכוין לברכו, אלא לבו היה לרבו. וצ"ע שלא יהא בזה גונב דעת הבריות. ועל חנם פי' כן, דלא קאמר אלא דאין כופלין לו שלום:
Tosafot on Gittin 62a:12:1.english: Peace to [my] master - Rashi explained [that Rav Kahana] did not intend to bless him, rather his heart was [directed] toward his [own] teacher. And this requires further study, lest this constitute deceiving people. And for naught did he explain [it] thus, for [the Gemara] only says that one may not double [the greeting of] peace to him:

Tosafot on Gittin 62a:3:1.hebrew: אין עושין חלת עם הארץ בטהרה - פי' בקונטרס: לפי שכבר נטמאה העיסה ביד ע"ה, וכהן יסמוך על הגבל שהוא חבר, ויהא סבור שהחלה טהורה. ולפירושו, אם יפריש ממקום אחר על אותה עיסה, חלתו טהורה. ונראה דבכל ענין אסור, דכל עיקר לא התירו אלא כדי חייו, ולא התירו אלא היכא שנוטל שכר מכל העיסה; אבל משום שכר חלה גרידא, משום ההיא פורתא לא התירו, דחיישינן דלמא נגע:
Tosafot on Gittin 62a:3:1.english: One may not prepare ḥalla for an am ha'aretz in [a state of] purity - Rashi explained: [This is] because the dough has already become ritually impure in the hand of the am ha'aretz, and a priest will rely on the kneader, who is a ḥaver, and will think that the ḥalla is pure. According to his explanation, if he separates [ḥalla] from elsewhere on behalf of that dough, his ḥalla is pure. However, it seems that it is forbidden in all cases, for fundamentally they only permitted [it for the kneader's] livelihood, and they only permitted [it] where he receives payment for the entire dough; but for the payment for ḥalla alone — for that small amount they did not permit [it], because we are concerned lest [the am ha'aretz] touch [it]:

Tosafot on Gittin 62a:4:1.hebrew: ומניחה בכליו של חבר - נראה דלא נקט כפישא ואנחותא, לפי שהן פשוטי כלי עץ ולא חזו לזיתים:
Tosafot on Gittin 62a:4:1.english: And places it in the vessel of a ḥaver - It appears that [the baraita] did not mention kefisha or anḥuta because they are flat wooden utensils and are not suitable for olives:
